questions.title: Does a number need a "+" or "00" to count as having a country code?
questions.question: If a merchant types a number without a leading "+" or "00" (for example "1-415-555-0123"), do we treat its first digits as the country code and save it in the standard format, or does it fail the country-code check and get saved exactly as typed?

options.label: Treat the first digits as the country code and save it in the standard format ("+14155550123")
options.clarification: A leading "+" or "00" is not required: the first digits the merchant typed are treated as the country code, so any number with 7 to 15 digits passes the check and is saved as "+" followed by its digits.

options.label: It fails the check and is saved exactly as typed ("1-415-555-0123")
options.clarification: A number counts as including a country code only if it starts with "+" or the international prefix "00"; any number without one fails the check and is saved exactly as the merchant typed it.
